reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
Box is a public company, ticker BOX, CIK 0001372612, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Redwood City, California. Its site presents it as an Intelligent Content Management platform for accessing, sharing, editing, and co-creating unstructured content such as sales presentations, product specs, employee handbooks, lease agreements, and finance documents, with enterprise security and compliance built in. The company describes Box AI as letting users tap leading models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google for real-time summaries, analysis, and recommendations, and Box AI Studio as a way to customize agents. It also describes a drag-and-drop workflow builder, AI-driven security with deep learning-based malware detection, automated classification and access controls, AI-driven e-signature workflows, and support for requirements such as GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA. Box says it was named a Leader with the highest scores possible in 13 criteria, including innovation, vision, security, and AI/ML.

The record tracks one product, Box AI, listed under Notes, Knowledge and Meetings and described as enterprise content AI with metadata, governance, compliance, and retention policies. Filing data shows a 10-K for the period ending 2026-01-31 with revenue of $1,177,253,000.

Litigation exposure is recorded for California, with a count of 281. A set of MCP server entries is also held with the Box record, including ai.clize/inbox, ai.smithery/smithery-toolbox, ai.smithery/cindyloo-dropbox-mcp-server, and bot.mailbox/mailbox. None of those descriptions identify Box as their publisher.
